note: Primitive drive-in campground on the north shore of Pickwick Lake off TN-128 near Savannah (940 Branum Lane), a satellite of Pickwick Landing State Park. Sites 4-9 are tent-only (not accessible to a motorhome or trailer). The lakeshore row (1, 2, 10-19, 26-29) sits on open, gently sloping ground under scattered trees a short walk from the water. The bathhouse water is untreated well water. Playground, beach, boat ramp. --Claude
summary: Bruton Branch: park camping page, reserve.tnstateparks.com calendar + site photos + map, Google, Esri, 3DEP read. Open (Main Campground closed, Bruton open); $19 every night through 2026-12-31; year-round; no hookups; showers; 32 bookable sites (park says 33), 4-9 tent-only. Lakefront confirmed on named sites (1, 2, 10-19, 26-29). Stored max_rig_ft 50 cleared (no source). Pin ~1.7 km off.
flags: WATERFRONT lakefront CONFIRMED: the booking engine tags 1, 2, 10-19 and 26-29 'Water-front' (4-9 too, but tent-only) and 21-25, 30-34 'Water-view'. Site photos: 27 sits on open grass a few metres from the beach with the lake in full view; 15 and 19 look onto the lake through open, scattered trees (no understory). 3DEP: the loop ground is 127-128.5 m, 1-2.3 m above the 126.2 m summer pool, which runs ~20-50 m from the pads over a gentle open slope with a sand beach (e.g. 128.5 m at 35.070360,-88.193381 to pool at 35.069892,-88.193381, ~52 m from the inner loop road; east row 127.2 m at 35.070022,-88.192524 to pool ~37 m south) - passes the kayak test. All sites are sold by the night. Replacement waterfront evidence: 'reserve.tnstateparks.com tags Bruton Branch 1, 2, 10-19, 26-29 Water-front (4-9 tent-only); site photos 27/15/19 show open ground or scattered trees to the beach; 3DEP pads 127-128.5 m vs 126.2 m summer pool ~20-50 m away over a gentle slope (read 2026-11-25).'

PIN 35.05939,-88.18046 -> 35.0707,-88.1934 (~1.7 km; the stored pin is a residential lakeshore street SE of the campground; Google's pin and Esri imagery put the loop here, matching the park map). Stored waterfront evidence, if read at the old pin, described the wrong shore.
